title: The Coin
notes: This chunk builds a tight chain from the lost-coin parable through Caesar’s denarius, the minting of God’s people, the wisdom market, and the fish-mouth shekel into the Exodus census ransom. Law-positive density and symbol assembly are strong; the sockets, half-shekel math, and mouth-as-seal links land cleanly. Residual presenter staging remains in several instructional openers (Look at, Read without/with, notice, Mark the, Read the rest). One long absolute-phrase sentence on the Revelation firstborn parallel is compressed and benefits from a clean split. Scripture quotes and counts appear clean; no doctrine or quote wording needs change.

The chunk’s core strength is the tight member-for-member counterfeit of the temple census: name, number, rich/poor equality, plague inversion, and coin/mint vocabulary all land cleanly and assertively. Greek and Hebrew word studies (charagma, psēphos, chashav, alaphim/alluphim) stay dense and law-positive without padding. Residual defects are localized: an opening sentence fragment plus director cue and reader-meta, one broken relative clause on psēphos, an unclear “white one,” a verbless fragment after the Ezra citation, and light meta framing around gematria. No doctrine, quote, or symbol identification needs reopening; the fixes stay surgical.

proposals.old: Look at what the coin carries: an image and a name.
proposals.new: The coin carries an image and a name.
proposals.summary: Remove presenter cue; assert the claim directly.
proposals.rationale: “Look at” is residual director staging. The house style requires assertion without instructional openers.

proposals.old:
Read without the symbols, __“render unto Caesar”__ is a mirror — the tax-lover sees a command to pay, the tax-hater hears that everything is God's — and the scene shrinks to a clever escape from a trap.
Read with them, the sentence divides the world's whole estate by image and inscription: everything stamped by the beast returns to the beast, and everything stamped by God returns to God.
proposals.new:
Without the symbols, __“render unto Caesar”__ is a mirror — the tax-lover sees a command to pay, the tax-hater hears that everything is God's — and the scene shrinks to a clever escape from a trap.
With them, the sentence divides the world's whole estate by image and inscription: everything stamped by the beast returns to the beast, and everything stamped by God returns to God.
proposals.summary: Drop dual “Read” director cues; keep the contrast.
proposals.rationale: Parallel “Read without / Read with” is presenter staging. Stripping the verbs leaves the same contrast in author voice.

proposals.old: Solomon wrote the whole exchange out — and notice what the money is, and where the goods come from:
proposals.new: Solomon wrote the whole exchange out — what the money is, and where the goods come from:
proposals.rationale: “Notice” is an explicit forbidden presenter cue. The sentence already points at the quote; the staging word is surplus.

proposals.old: Mark the vocabulary of this market — silver, treasure, and a *mouth* — and carry it to the strangest coin-scene in the Gospels.
proposals.new: The vocabulary of this market is silver, treasure, and a *mouth*; the same terms open the strangest coin-scene in the Gospels.
proposals.summary: Replace “Mark… and carry it” staging with assertion.
proposals.rationale: “Mark the” and “carry it” are classic director cues. The rewrite keeps the vocabulary list and the forward link without instructing the reader.

proposals.old: Read the rest of the scene the same way: Peter, the fisher *of men* (Matthew 4:19), goes to the sym:sym-sea[sea] — the peoples and nations — and the *first* fish that comes up out of it carries silver in its *mouth*.
proposals.new: The rest of the scene works the same way: Peter, the fisher *of men* (Matthew 4:19), goes to the sym:sym-sea[sea] — the peoples and nations — and the *first* fish that comes up out of it carries silver in its *mouth*.
proposals.rationale: “Read the rest of the scene” is residual presenter staging. “Works the same way” keeps the parallel without the cue.

proposals.old: The womb the law watched opens again in Revelation, where the travailing woman __“brought forth a *man child*… and her child was *caught up unto God*, and to his throne”__ (Revelation 12:5), the dragon standing before her to devour him as Egypt's king stood before the firstborn — every redeemed firstborn a rehearsal of __“the *firstborn* of every creature”__ (Colossians 1:15).
proposals.new: The womb the law watched opens again in Revelation, where the travailing woman __“brought forth a *man child*… and her child was *caught up unto God*, and to his throne”__ (Revelation 12:5). The dragon stands before her to devour him as Egypt's king stood before the firstborn — every redeemed firstborn a rehearsal of __“the *firstborn* of every creature”__ (Colossians 1:15).
proposals.summary: Split the long absolute-phrase sentence at the natural seam.
proposals.rationale: The trailing absolute (“the dragon standing…”) overloads one sentence and obscures the claim. Two short sentences preserve every link and improve assembly.

proposals.old: Appointed how, Exodus records to the shekel: __“of the hundred talents of silver were *cast the sockets of the sanctuary*, and the sockets of the vail; … a talent for a socket”__ (Exodus 38:25-27) — a half-shekel a head for 603,550 counted men, melted into the foundations.
proposals.new: Exodus records the appointment to the shekel: __“of the hundred talents of silver were *cast the sockets of the sanctuary*, and the sockets of the vail; … a talent for a socket”__ (Exodus 38:25-27) — a half-shekel a head for 603,550 counted men, melted into the foundations.
proposals.rationale: “Appointed how,” reads like a note fragment. The rewrite keeps the same evidence and density in ordinary author prose.

proposals.old:
Now the piece this symbol unlocks.
Revelation holds two enrollments, and nearly every reader studies the beast's *mark* in isolation — never suspecting that the mark is an enrollment at all.
Set the two side by side instead.
proposals.new:
The coin unlocks the mark.
Revelation holds two enrollments. The beast's *mark* is almost always studied in isolation — never as an enrollment at all.
The two stand side by side.
proposals.summary: Remove fragment, reader-meta, and director imperative.
proposals.rationale: “Now the piece…” is a sentence fragment and presenter cue; “nearly every reader” is meta-talk; “Set the two…” is a director command. Assert the two enrollments directly.

proposals.old: The Greek verb is _psēphizō_ — to tally with a _psēphos_, the pebble ancient counting and voting were done with — and its only other use in Scripture is a cost-tally: __“which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and *counteth the cost*?”__ (Luke 14:28).
proposals.new: The Greek verb is _psēphizō_ — to tally with a _psēphos_, the pebble with which ancient counting and voting were done — and its only other use in Scripture is a cost-tally: __“which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and *counteth the cost*?”__ (Luke 14:28).
proposals.summary: Repair the broken relative clause on psēphos.
proposals.rationale: “the pebble ancient counting and voting were done with” lacks the relative pronoun and is ungrammatical; “with which” restores the clause without changing meaning.

proposals.old: The Hebrew Revelation names what the white one holds: the overcomer receives __“a *good testimony*, and in this testimony a *new name* written”__ — God's vote cast *for* a man, his sealed entry in the census of the sealed; the mark is the vote against, carried on the flesh.
proposals.new: The Hebrew Revelation names what the white stone holds: the overcomer receives __“a *good testimony*, and in this testimony a *new name* written”__ — God's vote cast *for* a man, his sealed entry in the census of the sealed; the mark is the vote against, carried on the flesh.
proposals.rationale: “the white one” is unclear on first read; “white stone” keeps the exact referent already established two sentences earlier.

proposals.old:
Most reach for gematria here, as though Revelation were asking for another candidate whose letters add to 666.
This chapter's claim is different: Revelation 13 is not first a gematria problem but a covenant census problem.
proposals.new:
Gematria is the usual reach here, as though Revelation were asking for another candidate whose letters add to 666.
Revelation 13 is not first a gematria problem but a covenant census problem.
proposals.summary: Drop reader-meta and “this chapter’s claim” framing.
proposals.rationale: “Most reach” and “This chapter’s claim is different” are meta-talk about readers and the book itself; the revised lines assert the same contrast without the staging.

proposals.old: A count filed under the name that owns it, in the register of those *coming out of Babylon*.
proposals.new: The count is filed under the name that owns it, in the register of those *coming out of Babylon*.
proposals.summary: Supply a finite verb to the post-quote fragment.
proposals.rationale: “A count filed…” is a verbless fragment after the Ezra citation; “The count is filed” restores a complete sentence while preserving the claim.
